claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been produced in a hierarchical-heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A hybrid surrogate can combine reduced-order physics estimates with descriptors of local phase distribution, interfaces, and chemical-fluctuation gradients.
Training on tensile and fracture-test data can calibrate predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
Machine-learning surrogate models have predicted room-temperature yield strength in refractory high-entropy alloys with an average error of about 11%.
Ab initio and molecular-dynamics calculations are too time-consuming for high-throughput alloy-structure prediction.
CALPHAD modeling for high-entropy alloys can require significant computing resources and can be limited by unreliable databases.
Phase connectivity, local elastic-modulus distributions, interfaces, and composition gradients govern stress distribution and crack initiation in hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Explicit hierarchical-microstructure descriptors will allow the surrogate to capture the influence of microstructural heterogeneity on mechanical response.
The hybrid surrogate will bypass exhaustive atomistic or full CALPHAD simulations.
Explicit hierarchical descriptors will make predictions more accurate than CALPHAD, first-principles, and standard machine-learning workflows lacking those descriptors.
The hybrid model will reduce prediction error by roughly 20% relative to the baseline workflow.
The hybrid model will reduce computational time by more than an order of magnitude relative to the baseline workflow.
The model will reliably predict Young's modulus for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The model will reliably predict yield strength for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The model will reliably predict fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The model may become unreliable when the hierarchical microstructure lies significantly outside the training distribution.
The model may become unreliable when its descriptors omit features controlling fracture.
The proposed gains and the mapping from microstructure to fracture toughness remain to be prospectively validated.
